subject.title: macOS launchd Gateway still restarts via gateway-update/update.run; document and honor auto-update kill-switch

question: Should `OPENCLAW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1` suppress Gateway control-plane `update.run` managed-service handoffs on launchd/headless deployments, or remain limited to configured `update.auto` background applies?
rationale: The code boundary is clear, but changing the env variable would broaden a documented background-auto-update kill-switch into explicit control-plane update behavior that may be user- or UI-triggered.

options.title: Extend the existing kill-switch
options.body: Block supervised Gateway-originated managed `update.run` handoffs before the restart handoff is created when `OPENCLAW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1`, while leaving explicit shell `openclaw update` available.

options.title: Keep the current split
options.body: Document that `OPENCLAW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE` only blocks configured `update.auto` applies and leave explicit `update.run` reliability under the broader launchd update-run tracker.

options.title: Add a separate explicit-update guard
options.body: Keep the current env semantics and introduce a new documented operator policy for disabling Gateway/UI/agent-triggered package update restarts.

recommendation.title: Extend the existing kill-switch
recommendation.body: Block supervised Gateway-originated managed `update.run` handoffs before the restart handoff is created when `OPENCLAW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1`, while leaving explicit shell `openclaw update` available.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is product/API scope for updater and Gateway restart behavior, and Peter's history covers both the core updater foundation and Gateway update restart flow.
